A recent market intelligence report states that Apple will pay four times more for memory in the iPhone 18 Pro compared to last year's model.

TrendForce indicates that Apple will not pass on the full cost to consumers and will increasingly rely on services revenue to offset rising hardware production costs...

Apple announced in June that it was significantly raising prices on most of its products, stating it had done everything possible to delay the increases but had no other options.

Apple did not raise prices on current iPhones at the time, but that is expected to change next week. TrendForce noted a sharp increase in memory costs for the new models.

Apple is not expected to pass on the full increase in memory costs to iPhone pricing. Current estimates suggest the iPhone 18 Pro will be priced approximately $100 higher than the iPhone 17 Pro.

The reason is that a significant price hike would cause even Apple's most loyal fans to upgrade their devices less frequently. TrendForce noted that Apple would not want to sacrifice its ongoing growth, while also pointing out that a weak macroeconomic environment is making consumers more cautious with their spending.

The company predicts that Apple's first foldable phone, the iPhone Ultra, could have a starting price as high as $2,299, with top configurations potentially exceeding $3,000.
